Typing practice

Type the text exactly. Timer starts with your first key.

Text to type: A cafe order can start with a drink name. Tea and coffee are two drinks people can order. A drink can be hot or cold. The size is another part of the order. A small cup holds less than a large cup. The drink and the size go together in an order. Mara works at a cafe and makes the drinks. One person wants hot tea in a small cup. Mara hears the drink name, but not the size. She asks about the size before she makes it. The person says small, and the order is clear. Mara makes the hot tea in a small cup.

Roleplay

Ask for a Small Cup

You

Sorry, a small cup, please.

Mara

Oh, sorry! A small tea?

You

Yes, a small tea to go.

Mara

Here is a small cup. I will make your tea now.

You

Thank you.

Mara

Here is your small tea to go.

You

Yes, that is right.

Speak

Your Turn at the Counter

  1. Ordering at the counter: You want a small hot tea to go. Mara is the barista, and the cafe takes cash and cards. Give your full order and say how you want to pay. Then Mara puts out a large cup. Ask for the right size.

    Need a starting line?

    Helpful clue: Give the drink, size, and place first. Then say cash or card. Ask for a small cup at the end.

What you can do now

Final Reflection

  1. A cafe order includes a drink and a size. Cash and cards are ways to pay. What drink would you order, and how would you pay?

    Need a starting line?
    • What would you say if the cup was the wrong size?

Reading

Drinks and Size

A cafe order can start with a drink name.

Tea and coffee are two drinks people can order.

A drink can be hot or cold.

The size is another part of the order.

A small cup holds less than a large cup.

The drink and the size go together in an order.

Mara works at a cafe and makes the drinks.

One person wants hot tea in a small cup.

Mara hears the drink name, but not the size.

She asks about the size before she makes it.

The person says small, and the order is clear.

Mara makes the hot tea in a small cup.

Reading

Cash or Card

People pay for their drinks when they order at this cafe.

Cash is money in coins or notes.

A card is another way to pay here.

Mara takes both cash and cards at the counter.

One person orders a coffee and wants to pay.

The person has a card but has no cash.

Mara says a card is fine for this order.

The person uses the card to pay for the coffee.

Mara says the payment is done, so the person stops.

A receipt shows what the person bought and paid.

The person takes the receipt and the coffee.

The drink is paid for, and the order is complete.

Reading

For Here or To Go

Some people drink their tea at a cafe table.

Other people take their drinks away from the cafe.

For here means the person will stay at the cafe.

To go means the person will take the drink away.

Mara asks this before she gives someone a drink.

One person orders a small tea to go.

Mara puts a large cup on the counter by mistake.

The person sees the cup before Mara makes the tea.

The order was for a small tea, not a large tea.

The person asks for a small cup.

Mara takes a small cup and makes the tea.

The person takes the small tea away from the cafe.
